transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Maya (Wayfinder Procurement), Evan (Wayfinder Counsel), Priya (Wayfinder Eng), Tom (Wayfinder CISO)

Summary (auto): Quick conformance sprint to close outstanding legal and procurement questions before pilot sign-off. Some crosstalk around SLA definitions and KMS integration.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everybody, thanks for making time. quick round robin — we'll run ~40 minutes then wrap with next steps. Maya, Evan, Priya, Tom — you good?
[00:14] Maya: Yeah thanks Jordan. We want to get through the MSA exceptions and make sure the DPA maps to our residency needs. Also pricing approval timeline is... tight.
[00:28] Evan: From legal side I'll call out a handful of DPA items: subprocessor list, breach notification window, and deletion/return obligations. We'll put specifics on the redline.
[00:40] Sofia: hi all, jumping in on technical constraints — for the pilot Wayfinder wants private deployment in AWS eu-west-1, with KMS integration and audit logs retained 13 months. We can support that but need to confirm exact log payloads.
[01:05] Priya: yes, we will need the schema for audit logs — especially token-level metadata and request hashes for forensics. Also need to know if KV cache persists across restarts.
[01:25] Liam: quick note from success: timeline matters — procurement wants a signed PO by mid-July to meet Q3 rollout.
[01:40] Tom: security is concerned about access patterns. If there's any managed key access, we need proof of no key exfiltration and attestation of HSM usage.
[02:10] Jordan: understood. quick real talk on MSA: we typically accept most redlines but there are a few revenue-impacting asks like indemnity caps and IP warranty clauses. Evan, are you able to share the customer's 'non-negotiables'?
[02:31] Evan: Our main non-starters are long breach notification windows and anything that prevents us from requiring subprocessor approvals. We can be flexible on indemnity but not unlimited liability.
[02:50] Sofia: to address the breach window — Redwood's incident timeline is 72 hours for initial notification and detailed report in 10 business days. We can add contractual language to that effect.
[03:07] Maya: 72 hours is acceptable if we get a SLA credit mechanism for severe incidents, otherwise procurement will push back.
[03:22] Jordan: about SLA credits — our standard is tiered credits tied to p99 latency and availability. We can share sample SLA metric definitions.
[03:36] Priya: can you give a concrete p99 target for the dedicated configuration? Our workload is interactive query-based, 8-16 token bursts, SLOs are strict.
[03:50] Sofia: on Dedicated we aim for p95 < 80ms and p99 < 220ms for short sequences under typical concurrency. But we should run the customer's sample to validate. Those numbers vary by model variant and quantization.
[04:12] Tom: do you have historical variance numbers and SLO burn-rate math? We need to present to our risk committee.
[04:22] Sofia: yes we can package the burn-rate analysis — we'll include traces and percentile breakdowns.
[04:30] Jordan: pricing — Maya, what's the procurement approval path? is it centralized?
[04:38] Maya: Finance needs a two-step: initial pricing approval from sourcing, legal sign-off on MSA/DPA, then final PO. We need a committed monthly spend number to budget.
[04:52] Jordan: we can propose a pilot package: 3-week pilot with reserved capacity equivalent and a conversion credit toward committed monthly. We'll include a pricing worksheet.
[05:08] Evan: DPA specifics — data residency clause: we require all production customer data to remain in eu-west-1; backups must also reside in EU. Any logs that include customer identifiers must be stored and processed in EU only.
[05:32] Sofia: technically we can run Private in your VPC in eu-west-1 and bind to your KMS. Backups can be configured to the same region. There are edge cases around some telemetry that flows to our control plane — we can redact PII there and offer a version with no telemetry if needed.
[05:58] Tom: we want to see the list of telemetry fields. If you redact, what fields are removed and how do we know the redact is consistent?
[06:10] Sofia: we'll produce an audit schema and a sample scrubbed payload. for the strictest approach we can turn off telemetry entirely for the pilot and run all observability locally, though that reduces Redwood's ability to surface product-level issues.
[06:35] Priya: for pilot perf benchmark — we need a 10k token run and also a simulated concurrent session test of 20 sessions. Can you do both?
[06:48] Sofia: yes, we'll perform a 10k end-to-end generation and a 20-concurrency churn test; include KV cache warm and cold runs. Expect raw trace + aggregated pXX results.
[07:03] Jordan: I'll also attach a pricing worksheet showing reserved vs burst pricing and conversion credits.
[07:10] Maya: procurement will want the worksheet before legal finalizes the MSA; they need to see spend commitments.
[07:20] Evan: on subprocessor list — can Redwood provide a current subprocessor map and commit to notice prior to adding new subprocessors?
[07:31] Jordan: yes we have a subprocessors document; we can add a 30-day notice clause for new subprocessors for enterprise customers.
[07:44] Evan: good. also deletion obligations — we need clear timelines after contract termination.
[07:50] Sofia: standard is 30 days for data deletion, with confirmation of deletion. We can extend to 60 days if needed.
[08:02] Tom: encryption at rest and in transit — we need E2E TLS and KMS-managed keys. Is HSM-backed KMS supported?
[08:12] Sofia: we support AWS KMS HSM-backed keys and customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS for enterprise tiers.
[08:29] Priya: for the PoC we want to validate KMS rotation and key access logs. can you share the format of key-use logs?
[08:38] Sofia: we'll share sample key-use records; they show key ID, operation, timestamp, and principal.
[08:45] Maya: procurement wants to confirm indemnity cap numbers. what's Redwood's standard limit?
[08:54] Jordan: typical is liability cap equal to 12 months of fees, with carve-outs for gross negligence and IP infringement. We are open to negotiation for enterprise deals.
[09:08] Evan: our counsel usually asks for a higher cap on IP claims — can you consider removing cap for IP indemnity?
[09:16] Jordan: removing cap on IP is difficult but we can consider specific language around third-party IP claims; we'll surface to legal.
[09:26] Liam: noting here — commercial wants the risk assessment to map to pricing concessions.
[09:32] Maya: also wanted to raise data retention for audit logs: 13 months is baseline; can Redwood support extended retention as an add-on?
[09:42] Jordan: yes, extended retention can be added as a paid add-on; we'll show pricing tiers.
[09:48] Priya: back to tech — what's your rollback policy if a deployed model variant shows quality regressions? we need automatic fallback to previous model.
[09:58] Sofia: Redwood supports model pinning and automated rollback policies — we can set canary windows and automatic fallback on key eval regressions. We'll include a sample policy.
[10:12] Tom: audit trail — we need immutable logs of who did model rollouts and when. Is that supported?
[10:19] Sofia: yes with RBAC and audit logs; we can export logs to your SIEM as well.
[10:26] Evan: any compliance reports or certificates you can share? SOC 2 Type II/ISO?
[10:32] Jordan: SOC 2 Type II in process — we have SOC 2 readiness artifacts and annual ISO27001 self-attestation. We'll share current reports and the compliance roadmap.
[10:47] Maya: procurement will want proof of penetration testing and third-party audit cadence.
[10:52] Jordan: we'll attach pentest summaries and timing for upcoming audits.
[11:00] (crosstalk)
[11:18] Sofia: quick note on telemetry again — if telemetry is disabled we'll still provide host-side metrics export so you can run internal monitors.
[11:30] Priya: thanks — that helps. Also can you confirm the expected timeline to deliver the benchmark artifacts?
[11:36] Sofia: aim 7 business days after we get sample dataset and access to a staging VPC — so roughly by 2026-07-07 if we get materials this week.
[11:48] Jordan: good. On pricing approvals — I'll send the worksheet and recommend the pilot credit & conversion terms. Can we align on target commit sizes?
[12:00] Maya: procurement would prefer a 12-month commit but for internal approval we'll consider a 6-month with conversion option. Need to see cost per token and committed discount levels.
[12:14] Jordan: we'll present 6- and 12-month tiers with breakpoints.
[12:22] Evan: legal will redline and return MSA/DPA — expect specific language on subprocessor notice, breach timelines, and deletion.
[12:31] Jordan: great — we'll action those. Anything else on compliance?
[12:36] Tom: just one more — do you offer certified data deletion attestation?
[12:42] Sofia: yes we can provide deletion certificates for enterprise.
[12:46] Maya: ok awesome.
[12:50] Jordan: Recap: Jordan to circulate MSA/DPA redlines & pricing worksheet by 7/3; Sofia to run perf benchmarks and share artifacts by 7/7; customer to supply residency and audit spec by 7/6; follow up meeting week of 7/9 to lock pricing and PO timing.
[13:10] Evan: sounds good, we'll get our redline back quickly.
[13:16] Priya: we'll get staging VPC access notes to you today.
[13:22] Liam: I'll set the follow-up calendar invite.
[13:26] (end of recorded transcript)

Notes: occasional transcription errors present — speaker turns labeled by role and may not perfectly align with voice. References: pricing worksheet link (shared in chat), MSA/DPA redline template (will be sent), perf benchmark plan (Sofia to deliver).
